reuse.why: Reuses the tolerance helper and shares range selection, but introduces getExpectedAmount alongside the existing getScheduledAmount abstraction without unifying them.

duplication.why: Most consumers share the new helper, but getExpectedAmount duplicates getScheduledAmount's missing, numeric, and ranged amount dispatch.

placement.why: Amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, tolerance remains in shared/rules.ts, and API serialization stays in the existing model.

scope.why: The edits are focused on schedule amount policy, its API exposure, and associated tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping amount helpers leave maintainers coordinating separate policy interfaces, with the API using the operator-unaware path.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts derives expectedAmount through getScheduledAmount rather than the operator-aware getExpectedAmount used by posting, forecasting, and previews.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts reshapes the existing missing/number/range dispatch into getExpectedAmount while retaining that dispatch in getScheduledAmount; extracting getRangedAmount shares only the range calculation.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount introduces an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch, while scheduleModel.toExternal remains on getScheduledAmount; the two shared helpers retain overlapping dispatch.
